new_entities.name: Daily sunscreen SPF 30+
aliases: habitual SPF 30 or higher sunscreen use
new_entities.description: Routine near-daily use of broad-spectrum sunscreen at SPF 30 or higher on sun-exposed skin.

new_entities.name: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
new_entities.description: Keratinocyte skin cancer arising from squamous cells of chronically sun-exposed skin.

edges.effect_quant: The original randomized trial found no clear effect on first SCC diagnosis but did find a significantly lower SCC tumour rate with daily sunscreen use, with a rate ratio of 0.61 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.81). Extended follow-up then showed about a 40% lower SCC tumour rate overall, with a rate ratio of 0.62 (95% CI 0.38 to 0.99).
edges.population: adults in sunny community settings using daily sunscreen on chronically exposed skin sites
edges.mechanism: Consistent sunscreen use reduces cumulative ultraviolet damage and mutational burden in keratinocytes, which matters more for long-latency SCC burden than for a single short-term first-event analysis.
edges.summary: This is one of the stronger prevention edges in dermatology because randomized and extended follow-up data both point the same way: daily sunscreen lowers squamous-cell-carcinoma burden over time. The cleanest benefit shows up in tumour counts and longer-term follow-up rather than a dramatic short-term drop in first-event incidence.
edges.caveats: This edge is stronger for cutaneous SCC than for basal cell carcinoma, and the data come from regular habitual use in a high-UV environment. It should not be oversold as absolute protection against all skin cancer.

evidence.notes: Daily sunscreen application and betacarotene supplementation in prevention of basal-cell and squamous-cell carcinomas of the skin: a randomised controlled trial.

effect_quant.comparator: squamous-cell carcinoma tumour incidence with daily sunscreen versus no daily sunscreen

evidence.citation: vanderPolsJC et al 2006 Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev
evidence.notes: Prolonged prevention of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin by regular sunscreen use.

effect_quant.comparator: long-term SCC tumour rate after former daily sunscreen assignment versus no daily sunscreen

evidence.citation: RonschH et al 2021 Curr Probl Dermatol
evidence.notes: The Preventive Value of Sun Protection.
